academictransfer:363696.description:
POLARIS doctoral network 
POLARIS is a European Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network focused on accelerating therapy development for leukodystrophies: rare genetic disorders affecting the brain's white matter. The network aims to strengthen the full translational pathway, from understanding disease mechanisms and developing disease models to preclinical therapy testing, clinical readiness and patient-informed treatment priorities.
To achieve this, POLARIS brings together expertise in leukodystrophy biology, advanced disease models, therapeutic innovation, biomarker development, clinical translation, patient engagement, and ethical, regulatory and health-economic aspects of therapy development. The network will train a cohort of doctoral candidates in an international and interdisciplinary environment, combining academic research, industry-based preclinical development, secondments, network-wide training and transferable-skills development.
For this position, the recruiting organisation is the Cyprus Institute of Neurology & Genetics (CING) in Nicosia, Cyprus. CING will employ you and you will be embedded in the POLARIS consortium. Academic supervision and disease-specific expertise will be provided by Prof Kleopa Kleopa and Dr Irene Sargiannidou from the Neuroscience Department.
 PhD project 
This doctoral project focuses on establishing isogenic iPSC-derived myelinating organoids as a physiologically relevant human in vitro model of Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease type 1 (PMLD1).
You will first test leading AAV capsids developed by Myrtelle Therapeutics Inc. in the in vitro model. You will assess their effects on myelination and oligodendrocyte survival. The most promising oligodendrocyte-targeting AAV variants will subsequently be tested in a PMLD1 mouse model to determine their therapeutic potential in vivo .
The project requires a strong foundation in neuroscience and an interest in both stem cell-based and animal research. Prior experience with cell culture techniques, behavioural and neurological phenotyping, and handling mice is an advantage.
Planned secondments will provide specialised training in establishing isogenic iPSC-derived myelinating organoids under the supervision of Dr Hendrick Rosewich in Tübingen, Germany. You will also have the opportunity to develop experience in patient advocacy, networking and research planning through a placement at the European Leukodystrophy Association (ELA).
The position is based in Nicosia, Cyprus, with academic enrolment through the Graduate School of the Cyprus Institute of Neurology and Genetics. You will pursue a PhD degree in Neuroscience.
You will contribute to the development and evaluation of gene therapy approaches for PMLD1. Your work includes:
 establishing and using isogenic iPSC-derived myelinating organoids as a human in vitro disease model;
 testing AAV variants and assessing their effects on myelination and oligodendrocyte survival;
 using a PMLD1 mouse model to evaluate the therapeutic potential of selected AAV variants in vivo ;
 applying behavioural and neurological phenotyping and other experimental approaches to assess disease mechanisms and treatment responses;
 analysing and interpreting experimental results and collaborating with researchers at CING and across the POLARIS consortium.
You will also participate in the POLARIS network-wide training programme and planned secondments. This gives you the opportunity to develop scientific and transferable skills in an international research environment.

REQUIREMENTS:
We are looking for a candidate with a Master's degree in Life Sciences, preferably in Neuroscience, and a strong interest in translational neuroscience and rare disease research.
Relevant experience may have been gained during an internship, thesis project or other research project. We are looking for:
 hands-on experience with in vivo mouse research;
 experience with behavioural or neurological phenotyping is an advantage;
 knowledge of animal welfare regulations and ethical principles, and an understanding of rigorous experimental design;
 a careful and reproducible approach, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills;
 good written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate in an interdisciplinary and international research environment.
Formal certification for working with laboratory animals is highly desirable.
Fluency in English, both written and spoken, is essential.
 Eligibility criteria 
Strict eligibility criteria under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network programme apply:
 At the time of recruitment, you must not already hold a doctoral degree.
 The MSCA mobility rule applies. Because CING is the recruiting organisation for this position, you must not have resided or carried out your main activity, such as work or study, in Cyprus for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date.
 You must be able and willing to work in an international training network, participate in network-wide training activities and undertake planned secondments with POLARIS partner organisations.

POLARIS doctoral network 
POLARIS is a European Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network focused on accelerating therapy development for leukodystrophies: rare genetic disorders affecting the brain's white matter. The network aims to strengthen the full translational pathway, from understanding disease mechanisms and developing disease models to preclinical therapy testing, clinical readiness and patient-informed treatment priorities.

The network will train a cohort of doctoral candidates in an international and interdisciplinary environment, combining academic research, industry-based preclinical development, secondments, network-wide training and transferable-skills development.
 PhD projects 
As a PhD candidate, you will develop and validate innovative MRI-based outcome measures to monitor disease activity and progression in cerebral adrenoleukodystrophy (C-ALD).
Two complementary PhD positions are available within the same multidisciplinary research programme at the Paris Brain Institute. Depending on your background, your work will focus on either the clinical and neuroradiological aspects of advanced MRI or the computational and image-analysis aspects of the research.
You will investigate the sensitivity, specificity, and clinical relevance of state-of-the-art quantitative MRI (qMRI) techniques for assessing disease activity and progression in C-ALD. Particular emphasis will be placed on techniques including diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and MR perfusion, which have shown promise as imaging biomarkers but require further validation in experimental and clinical settings.
You will process and analyse multimodal MRI and clinical data from paediatric and adult patients, combining clinical and neuroradiological expertise with computational and image-analysis approaches. The overall aim is to identify and validate robust imaging biomarkers that can improve the detection of disease activity, monitoring of disease progression, and development of clinically meaningful outcome measures for future therapeutic trials.
You will work closely with the other PhD candidate and with international experts in adult and paediatric leukodystrophies, neurology, neuroradiology, MRI, computational imaging, and patient engagement.
The two positions are complementary. One position is particularly suited to candidates with a background in clinical neurology or neuroradiology, while the other is suited to candidates with experience in computational sciences, image processing, and coding.
You will be supervised by Prof. Fanny Mochel and Dr. Caroline Sevin and will join the Metabolism, Immunity and Neurodegeneration (MIND) team at the Paris Brain Institute.
Planned secondments at the University of Amsterdam (the Netherlands), Eberhard Karls University of Tübingen (Germany), and one of two patient organisations—Alex TLC or the European Leukodystrophy Association (ELA)—will provide additional experience in next-generation MRI techniques, international research environments, and the psychosocial and patient-centred aspects of MRI screening in C-ALD.
The positions are based in Paris, France, with doctoral enrolment through the Sorbonne University doctoral school.
Leukodystrophies are inherited disorders affecting the brain's white matter and can cause a wide range of neurological symptoms and disability. They can present at different stages of life, from infancy to adulthood. Although genetic diagnosis has advanced considerably, genetic information alone does not always predict when disease will develop, how quickly it will progress, or how an individual patient will be affected.
 Cerebral adrenoleukodystrophy (C-ALD) is a common leukodystrophy and a progressive inflammatory demyelinating disorder. Regular clinical assessment and brain MRI are important for monitoring disease evolution.
Within this project, you will use C-ALD as a model to investigate whether advanced quantitative MRI techniques can provide sensitive and clinically meaningful measures of disease activity and progression. The project will contribute to the development of imaging biomarkers that could support clinical monitoring and future therapeutic trials.

REQUIREMENTS:
We are looking for candidates with an interest in neuroimaging, leukodystrophies, and clinical research, who would like to work in an international and multidisciplinary environment.
You:
 have excellent written and spoken English;
 have an interest in MRI and clinical research;
 are able to work independently and contribute actively to a multidisciplinary team;
 hold, or are expected to obtain before the start of the position, a Master's degree or equivalent relevant to the project;
 have a background in medicine, biomedical sciences, computer science, engineering, or a related discipline.
Depending on the PhD project, experience or an interest in neurology, neuroradiology, coding, computational science, image processing, or quantitative MRI may be particularly relevant.
The following would be an advantage:
 a medical degree, particularly in neurology or neuroradiology;
 experience in medical or scientific research;
 experience with coding, computational science, image processing, or quantitative MRI;
 experience working with clinical or neuroimaging data;
 basic knowledge of French.
The two positions are designed to complement each other. We welcome applications from candidates with either a clinical/neuroimaging profile or a computational/coding profile.
 Eligibility criteria 
Important, strict eligibility criteria according to MARIE SKLODOWSKA CURIE programs apply to applicants:
 You must not already hold a doctoral degree.
 At the time of the application deadline, you must have a Master's degree and must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in France for more than 12 months in the three years prior to the contract start date.
 You will participate in the network-wide training programme of POLARIS, which includes (international) training activities and planned secondments with POLARIS partner organizations throughout the EU.

academictransfer:363715.description:
How can de novo proteins be designed for enabling continuous biomolecular sensing? That’s your question!
 Information 
Biosensing technologies are being developed for the continuous monitoring of biomolecules in areas such as patient care, advanced biomanufacturing, the monitoring of ecological systems, and fundamental biological research. The heart of the continuous sensors are binder molecules that specifically and reversibly bind to the biomolecules of interest.
In this PhD project, you will explore a novel direction: you will develop and test binder molecules for continuous sensing using de novo protein design strategies. You will develop methodologies to design, make, screen, and test de novo proteins for incorporation in a particle-based continuous sensing platform with single-molecule resolution, called Biosensing by Particle Motion. The long-term goal is to develop a fast and flexible workflow for the rational design of continuous biomolecular sensors for diverse applications.
The project is a collaboration between the Molecular Biosensing and the Protein Engineering research groups at TU/e (see www.tue.nl/mbx and https://merkxlab.nl/ ). Their fields of expertise on continuous biosensing and protein engineering are at the forefront of science. The PhD project benefits from ongoing collaborations with research institutes and academic hospitals.
The research groups integrate laboratory-based and computational approaches for advancing sensor technology and bioengineering. The research is done in the context of the Institute for Complex Molecular Systems ( www.tue.nl/icms ). The groups initiated and organize the international competition on Sensors for Health ( www.sensus.org ) and the international symposium on Continuous Real-time Biomolecular Sensing ( https://sensus.org/symposium ).

REQUIREMENTS:
A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in molecular engineering sciences and/or analytical sciences, e.g. bioengineering, chemistry, biomedical engineering, analytical chemistry.
 A research-oriented attitude.
 Experimental and analytical skills, with interests in biomolecular engineering, biosensors, biochemistry, biophysics.
 Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team and interested in collaborating with industrial partners.
 Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students.
 Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level).

CONTRACT: 4 years

Lili’s Proto Lab (LPL) is de centrale makerspace van de faculteit Bètawetenschappen, waar kennis, faciliteiten en vakmanschap samenkomen. Hier werken studenten, onderzoekers en medewerkers interdisciplinair aan prototypes voor onderwijs en wetenschappelijk onderzoek. Als technisch coördinator ben je het eerste aanspreekpunt voor gebruikers en ondersteun je hen bij het ontwikkelen en realiseren van technische oplossingen. Naast de bètafaculteit bedienen we ook Geodesie, Diergeneeskunde en het UMC.
 Wat ga je doen? 
Lili’s Proto Lab is een veelzijdig uitgeruste makerspace met onder meer 3D-printers, lasersnijders en CNC-routers. Aangrenzend bevindt zich een professionele werkplaats van ruim 3.000 m² met hightech machines zoals draadvonken, vonkverspanen en 5-assig frezen.
Als technisch coördinator werk je samen met instrumentmakers, de LPL-manager, community manager en student-assistenten aan uiteenlopende projecten voor onderwijs en onderzoek. Studenten, onderzoekers en medewerkers uit verschillende disciplines ontwikkelen hier prototypes waarvoor jij ondersteuning, advies en begeleiding biedt. Geen dag is hetzelfde: de ene keer help je een student met een eerste prototype, de volgende keer werk je samen met onderzoekers aan een complexe technische oplossing of verzorg je een workshop. Dankzij de nauwe samenwerking met de afdeling Instrumentatie kun je gebruikmaken van specialistische kennis, geavanceerde apparatuur en uitgebreide productiefaciliteiten.
Daarnaast draag je bij aan de verdere professionalisering van het LPL. Je optimaliseert werkprocessen, denkt mee over de doorontwikkeling van faciliteiten en apparatuur en helpt projectresultaten toegankelijk te maken, in het kader van kennisdeling en het stimuleren van Open Science projecten in Lili’s Proto Lab.
Jouw kerntaken:
 Je denkt mee, adviseert en co-creëert bij de ontwikkeling en realisatie van innovatieve projecten en prototypes.
 Je begeleidt studenten, onderzoekers en medewerkers bij het ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en realiseren van technische oplossingen.
 Je verzorgt workshops en trainingen in fabricagevaardigheden, zoals 3D-ontwerp, 3D-printen, solderen en het werken met microcontrollers.
 Je deelt jouw technische kennis en ondersteunt gebruikers bij het veilig en effectief werken met zowel conventionele als digitale fabricagetechnieken en apparatuur.
 Je beheert de makerspace, inclusief materialen, outreach, apparatuur, onderhoud, kalibratie, bestellingen en een veilige werkomgeving.
 Je verbindt gebruikers, experts en de afdeling Instrumentatie en signaleert wanneer specialistische ondersteuning nodig is.
Kortom: een veelzijdige rol in een technische omgeving waar je de ruimte krijgt om te leren, anderen te begeleiden, maatwerkoplossingen te ontwikkelen en te werken met een breed scala aan hoogwaardige machines en technieken.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je bent nieuwsgierig en initiatiefrijk en voelt je op je gemak als verbindende schakel tussen de dienstverlening van de afdeling Instrumentatie (service, onderhoud en realisatie) en Lili's Proto Lab. Je stelt gemakkelijk prioriteiten, schakelt soepel tussen verschillende projecten en werkt op een constructieve manier samen met uiteenlopende teams.
Je hebt affiniteit met de bètawetenschappen en ervaring met een technische of laboratoriumomgeving. Je krijgt energie van het begeleiden, coachen en instrueren van studenten en medewerkers en weet anderen te inspireren om ideeën te ontwikkelen en innovatieve oplossingen te realiseren.
Dit breng jij verder mee:
 minimaal een hbo-diploma in een relevante technische richting;
 ruime ervaring met conventionele bewerkingstechnieken en machines (solderen, draaien, frezen, zagen, zetten en persen) en materialen (zoals hout, kunststoffen, aluminium en andere metalen);
 kennis van en interesse in digitale fabricagetechnieken, zoals 3D-modellering, 3D-printen en CNC-bewerking;
 basiskennis van elektronica en software, bijvoorbeeld Arduino, Raspberry Pi,, , Autodesk Fusion, sensoren en eenvoudige dataverwerking;
 goede communicatieve en organisatorische vaardigheden, waardoor je gebruikers weet te adviseren en samenwerking tussen verschillende disciplines stimuleert.

Het Cognitive Science & Artificial Intelligence Research Center van Tilburg University voert het  Secure Hardware Intelligence Extraction and Logic Deconstruction (SHIELD)-onderzoeksproject  uit. Dit wetenschappelijke project richt zich op AI-ondersteunde reverse engineering van geïntegreerde schakelingen, met toepassingen op het gebied van hardware assurance, dreigingsanalyse en inlichtingenanalyse.
 Het project wordt uitgevoerd binnen de onderzoekslijnen op het gebied van Deep Learning for Perception and Data Science en Safety and Security, in samenwerking met het Data Science Centre of Excellence van de Nederlandse Defensie Academie en het Nederlands Forensisch Instituut (NFI). In deze functie werk je op het raakvlak van computer vision, micro-elektronische analyse en hardwarebeveiliging. Je werkt onder begeleiding van onderzoekers binnen het Department of Intelligent Systems.
 Je wordt formeel aangesteld binnen het Department of Intelligent Systems (DIS) en werkt nauw samen met het Department of Computational Cognitive Science (DCS).
 Het project 
Het SHIELD-project is een samenwerking tussen Tilburg University, het Data Science Centre of Excellence van de Nederlandse Defensie Academie en het Nederlands Forensisch Instituut. Binnen het project wordt expertise op het gebied van kunstmatige intelligentie, micro-elektronische analyse en hardwarebeveiliging samengebracht. Het doel is om AI-ondersteunde methoden te ontwikkelen voor de reverse engineering van geïntegreerde schakelingen, ter ondersteuning van hardware assurance, dreigingsanalyse en processen voor inlichtingenanalyse.
 Binnen het project ontwikkel je een methodologie voor het analyseren van microscopische beelden met een hoge resolutie van geïntegreerde schakelingen. Daarbij combineer je computer vision, deep learning en technieken voor logische reconstructie. Je onderzoekt hoe verschillende beeldvormingstechnieken waaronder scanning electron microscopy (SEM), photon emission microscopy (PEM) en focused ion beam (FIB) imaging - met AI kunnen worden gecombineerd om chipstructuren op nanoschaal te reconstrueren en de werking van een chip af te leiden uit de fysieke lay-out.
 Een belangrijke uitdaging is om betrouwbare structurele en logische informatie te verkrijgen uit complexe halfgeleiderarchitecturen, terwijl de beschikbare beeldgegevens te maken kunnen hebben met ruis, beperkte beeldkwaliteit en andere praktische beperkingen.
 Je richt je in het bijzonder op de volgende drie hoofdtaken:
 (a) het ontwikkelen van deep-learningpipelines voor het segmenteren van meerdere chip-lagen en het classificeren van transistors op nanoschaal op basis van microscopische beelden;
 (b) het ontwikkelen van op grafen gebaseerde inferentiemodellen waarmee hogere-level logische blokken kunnen worden gereconstrueerd en afwijkende structuren kunnen worden geïdentificeerd die mogelijk wijzen op Hardware Trojans;
 (c) het evalueren van methoden voor het uitlezen en reconstrueren van geheugeninhoud, het analyseren van kwetsbaarheden en het reconstrueren van logische structuren op basis van beeldgegevens die rechtstreeks zijn gekoppeld aan de fysieke chipstructuur.
 Je onderzoekt hoe AI-gestuurde analyse het huidige, grotendeels handmatige reverse engineeringproces kan automatiseren. Daarbij ontwikkel je methoden om relevante kenmerken uit microscopische beelden te halen en de onderliggende structuur van een chip te interpreteren. De ontwikkelde methoden moeten bovendien robuust zijn tegen ruis, obfuscatie en verschillen tussen chiparchitecturen. Omdat het onderzoek zich op het snijvlak van wetenschappelijke innovatie en hardwarebeveiliging bevindt, is er veel aandacht voor een verantwoorde omgang met gevoelige datasets en forensische randvoorwaarden. Je werkt aan methodologische vernieuwing en houdt daarbij rekening met de eisen die gelden voor onderzoek naar gevoelige hardware en data. Het uiteindelijke doel van het project is het ontwikkelen van een reproduceerbare proof-of-conceptmethodologie waarmee geïntegreerde schakelingen op grotere schaal kunnen worden geanalyseerd. De methodologie moet toepasbaar zijn voor zowel defensieve hardwareverificatie als inlichtingenanalyse van in beslag genomen elektronische apparatuur. Je onderzoekt de wetenschappelijke validiteit en beperkingen van de ontwikkelde methoden en draagt bij aan open-accesspublicaties en technische documentatie. Het SHIELD-project heeft een toekomstgerichte onderzoeksvisie en wil bijdragen aan de versterking van langetermijncapaciteiten op het gebied van betrouwbare hardware, halfgeleidersouvereiniteit en cyber-elektromagnetische weerbaarheid.
 Je werkt voornamelijk binnen de AI-onderzoeksinfrastructuur van Tilburg University. Je houdt je daar bezig met algoritmeontwikkeling, het trainen van modellen en het valideren van de ontwikkelde methoden. De experimentele validatie en de beeldgegevens komen voort uit samenwerkingen met gespecialiseerde forensische en defensiepartners. Het Nederlands Forensisch 

REQUIREMENTS:
Jouw kwalificaties 
 Je hebt een afgeronde universitaire masteropleiding in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computational Neuroscience, Natuurkunde of een vergelijkbare opleiding met een sterke kwantitatieve component.
 Je beschikt over sterke programmeervaardigheden in Python en hebt aantoonbare ervaring met machine-learning- en deep-learningframeworks, zoals PyTorch of TensorFlow. Ervaring met computer vision en beeldanalyse is bij voorkeur aanwezig.
 Je beschikt over sterk analytisch denkvermogen en bent goed in het structureren van complexe vraagstukken. Je bent in staat om complexe systemen te abstraheren, de kern van een onderzoeksprobleem te identificeren en methodologisch onderbouwde oplossingen te ontwikkelen.
 Je kunt complexe technische onderwerpen helder uitleggen, zowel schriftelijk als mondeling, in het Engels. Daarnaast beschik je over goede academische schrijfvaardigheden en heb je interesse in het delen van onderzoeksresultaten via open wetenschappelijke publicaties.

Het Willem Pompe Instituut zoekt een enthousiaste universitair docent straf(proces)recht. Je geeft onderwijs en doet onderzoek op het terrein van het straf(proces)recht. Voor deze vacature nodigen we alle specialisaties binnen het brede domein van het straf(proces)recht uit om te solliciteren. We horen graag welke expertise jij het Willem Pompe Instituut te bieden hebt en hoe je je verder wilt ontwikkelen. Wel is van belang dat je in staat bent over de hele breedte van het straf(proces)recht onderwijs te verzorgen.
 Wat ga je doen? 
Het Willem Pompe Instituut voor Strafrechtswetenschappen – de afdeling Strafrecht van het departement Rechtsgeleerdheid van de Faculteit Recht, Economie, Bestuur en Organisatie (REBO) van de Universiteit Utrecht – is op zoek naar een collega met ervaring in universitair onderwijs en onderzoek op het gebied van het straf- en strafprocesrecht. De functie bestaat in beginsel uit 65% onderwijs en 35% onderzoek.
Je wordt ingezet in het onderwijs in de bachelor- en mastervakken van de afdeling Strafrecht. Het betreft voornamelijk strafrechtelijk onderwijs in de Nederlandstalige bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid (verplichte vakken en keuzevakken (soms Engelstalig)), in de Nederlandstalige master Strafrecht en/of de Engelstalige master European Criminal Justice in a Global Context . Voorts is inzet mogelijk in de Engelstalige masters Law and Technology in Europe of Law and Sustainability in Europe . Daarnaast begeleid je scripties in de bachelor- en masterfase. Ook vervul je overige onderwijsgerelateerde taken, zoals onderwijscoördinatie, tutoraat (voor eerstejaarsstudenten), voorlichting en het ontwikkelen en/of reviseren van onderwijs.
Je verricht onderzoek op jouw vakgebied, dat aansluit bij één van de onderzoeksprogramma’s van het departement. Deze zijn ondergebracht in de volgende vijf onderzoeksgroepen: het Montaigne Centrum voor Rechtsstaat en Rechtspleging, het Utrecht Centre for Regulation and Enforcement in Europe (RENFORCE), het Utrecht Centre for Accountability and Liability Law (UCALL), het Utrecht Centre for European Research into Family Law (UCERF) en het Utrecht Centre for Water, Oceans and Sustainability Law (UCWOSL). Wil jij bijdragen aan de wetenschap én de praktijk van kansengelijkheid in het onderwijs? Als universitair docent Onderwijswetenschappen combineer je hoogwaardig onderzoek naar onderwijs en sociale ongelijkheid met inspirerend onderwijs. Je werkt samen met een ambitieus team van onderzoekers en docenten en draagt bij aan wetenschappelijke én maatschappelijke impact.
Als universitair docent Onderwijswetenschappen verricht je zelfstandig wetenschappelijk onderzoek naar onderwijs en sociale ongelijkheid binnen het onderzoeksprogramma Educational Sciences van het Behavioural Science Institute (BSI). Je publiceert onderzoeksresultaten in nationale en internationale peer-reviewed tijdschriften en werkt samen met collega's aan gezamenlijke onderzoeksprojecten en interdisciplinaire vraagstukken.
Je speelt een actieve rol in het verwerven van extern gefinancierd onderzoek door het ontwikkelen en schrijven van subsidieaanvragen bij nationale en Europese fondsen, zoals het Nationaal Kennisinstituut Onderwijs en Horizon Europe. Daarnaast bouw en onderhoud je een relevant nationaal en internationaal wetenschappelijk netwerk.
Je draagt bij aan de maatschappelijke impact van wetenschappelijk onderzoek door wetenschap, beleid en praktijk met elkaar te verbinden. Daarbij neem je deel aan projecten waarin co-creatie en citizen science een belangrijke plaats innemen. Ook lever je een bijdrage aan de zichtbaarheid en positionering van het onderzoek van de afdeling, in het bijzonder in de regio Zuidoost-Nederland.
Naast je onderzoekstaken verzorg je onderwijs binnen de bachelor- en masteropleidingen Pedagogische Wetenschappen en Onderwijswetenschappen. Je geeft onder meer hoorcolleges en werkgroepen en begeleidt bachelor- en masterscripties. Daarnaast ontwikkel en actualiseer je onderwijsmateriaal en lever je een actieve bijdrage aan curriculumontwikkeling en kwaliteitsverbetering van het onderwijs. Je werkt nauw samen met collega-docenten en draagt bij aan de organisatie en coördinatie van onderwijsactiviteiten binnen de opleidingen.
Tot slot neem je actief deel aan teamoverleggen en facultaire activiteiten en draag je, afhankelijk van de behoeften van de afdeling, bij aan taken op het gebied van organisatie, kwaliteitszorg en externe relaties.

Why does heat affect people differently? Join the Horizon Europe HARARA project to explore the lived realities of urban heat and shape inclusive climate adaptation solutions. 
Job description 
This postdoctoral position is part of the HARARA project, a Horizon Europe Mission initiative funded by the European Commission. HARARA examines both the objective and subjective experiences of heat among migrantised communities in Antwerp and Rotterdam. The project brings together researchers from Erasmus University Rotterdam, the University of Antwerp, and Delft University of Technology, alongside civil society partners Empact vzw and Cultuurwerkplaats Tarwewijk, to develop a holistic understanding of the impacts of urban heat. By exploring how people experience, interpret, and respond to heat-related challenges, the consortium aims to contribute to the development of inclusive and effective climate adaptation solutions.
As a postdoctoral researcher, you will be primarily responsible for conducting a comparative analysis of heat impacts in Antwerp and Rotterdam. You will analyse and correlate objective measurements of indoor temperature and humidity with survey data on residents’ perceptions and experiences of heat, collected from 75 households in each city. In addition, you will map and assess existing inclusive local climate adaptation practices in both cities and contribute to the development and refinement of policy frameworks and community-based adaptation strategies in collaboration with the project’s civil society partners.
You will be based within the section of Environmental Technology and Design (ETD). ETD contributes to inter- and transdisciplinary, context-driven and problem/solution-focused research and education for the sake of a better environment. It involves a collaborative design and engineering approach, with social-and environmental-based methods and techniques as operative instruments, as well as the development and application of advanced urban data science and geospatial information technologies to support this primary aim. Research and education blend environmental technology, urban ecology, citizen participation and environmental behaviour at different scales. There is a strong emphasis on the interaction of these fields in terms of theories, methods and techniques, as well as their application via concepts, strategies and spatial interventions, as a significant part of ETD's research portfolio concerns applied science for and often with public and private partners.
Job requirements 
We are looking for a highly motivated researcher with:
 A PhD in a relevant discipline, such as urbanism, environmental sciences, public health, sociology, or a related field.

 An interest in translating research findings into practical and policy-relevant recommendations.
 Excellent writing and communication skills in English. Knowledge of Dutch is an advantage, given the collaboration with local partners and field sites in Antwerp and Rotterdam.

Job description 
The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays an important role in determining how tumors respond to radiotherapy. Features such as stromal composition, hypoxia, and cellular senescence can contribute to radioresistance and may therefore represent potential therapeutic targets.
In this PhD project, you will investigate how modulation of the TME can enhance the response to radiotherapy. The project will combine patient-derived models and in vivo tumor models to study how different TME characteristics contribute to treatment response and to explore potential strategies to target these mechanisms. A range of complementary preclinical approaches is used, including hypoxia modulation, targeting of senescent cells or cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs), (image-guided) radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibition. Treatment response and underlying mechanisms will be assessed through readouts such as DNA damage and repair, tumor growth and characterization of the TME. The precise experimental approaches will be guided by the scientific findings and direction of the project.

REQUIREMENTS:
Profile 
 Requirements 
 An MSc degree in Biomedical Sciences, Biology, Cancer Biology, or a related field, or an equivalent degree,
 A strong interest in preclinical cancer research,
 Motivated to investigate biological mechanisms underlying treatment response,
 Curious, enthusiastic about experimental science, and enjoy working in an interdisciplinary research environment.
Experience with molecular and cellular biology, tumor biology, radiobiology or immunology is an advantage. Experience with preclinical animal models is welcome, and candidates holding an Article 9 certificate for working with experimental animals are especially encouraged to apply.

academictransfer:363769.description:
The Department of Mathematics of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam welcomes applications for a fully-funded, 4-year PhD position in causal inference.
You will join the “Safe Causal Inference” consortium. Causal inference studies what assumptions are needed, and which methods you can use when those assumptions are met, to reliably conclude that “A causes B” and not just “A is correlated with B”. The consortium aims to incorporate all uncertainties into causal inferences, combining information obtained under alternative assumptions. In a team of 8 PhD researchers and 5 Principal Investigators located throughout the Netherlands, you’ll join us in developing a novel, iterative approach to causal inference that combines the strengths of subject-matter knowledge and the flexibility of data-driven algorithms.
You will work on the subproject “Triangulation of performance assessment methods for conditional causal quantities”. This PhD project investigates how to reliably assess the performance of estimators of conditional causal effects (such as CATE estimators and predictions under interventions). The core problem is that evaluating an estimator requires counterfactual outcomes in the evaluation dataset, but deriving those outcomes itself relies on causal assumptions, meaning the evaluation can be just as assumption-dependent as the estimator it's meant to assess.
You will examine whether combining evaluation results across different datasets, different causal assumptions, and different evaluation approaches (counterfactual, factual, and benchmarking against trials) leads to a more complete and reliable picture of a causal relationship. The goal is to develop a framework that helps data analysts choose the best evaluation strategy depending on which assumptions they are willing to make.
You will be jointly supervised by dr. Stéphanie van der Pas (VU), dr. Nan van Geloven (LUMC) and dr. Jeremy Labrecque (ErasmusMC). Your main working location will be the Mathematics department at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, where you will join dr. Stéphanie van der Pas’ research group on causal inference.
We are an inclusive, interdisciplinary group, and diversity and internationalism is at the heart of our research principles, as well as our teaching practice.
The preferred starting date is: as soon as possible, ideally before 01.02.2027.
Applications from all groups currently under-represented in academic posts are especially encouraged. We particularly welcome applications from women and people with an ethnic minority background.
 Your duties 
 doing research towards writing a PhD thesis
 teaching tasks (roughly 15% of your time), for instance supervising exercise classes

REQUIREMENTS:
a (prospective) MSc. degree in Mathematics, Statistics or Econometrics (or an equivalent thereof)
 good communication skills in English
Priority will be given to candidates with:
 a strong background in statistics
 experience with causal inference
 affinity with programming in R or python

CONTRACT: 1 year

Are you eager to dive into cutting-edge neuromodulation and real-world symptom monitoring? 
As a research assistant in our team, you will be running TMS sessions, working with intensive longitudinal data from daily life, and contributing to a new, state-informed approach to brain stimulation. This position offers the unique opportunity to work at the intersection of neuroscience, data science, and clinical research, with room for creativity, technical exploration, and meaningful impact. Here you'll have the chance to help deliver an iTBS protocol targeting the left prefrontal cortex, to model how cognitive fatigue fluctuates from moment to moment, and to explore who responds to stimulation and when. Curious minds are very welcome.
 Context  
In this project, members of the Cognitive Neuropsychology Department at Tilburg University aim to bridge real-time symptom monitoring in daily life with a pilot neuromodulation design, to better understand when and for whom stimulation may be most effective. By identifying dynamic fatigue profiles in students with elevated fatigue and relating them to short-term response to iTBS, the project lays the groundwork for more personalized, state-informed brain stimulation in clinical populations experiencing "mental fog".
 Your position  
As a Research Assistant, you will support an ongoing pilot project that combines ecological momentary assessment (EMA) with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), with the broader goal of understanding cognitive fatigue as a dynamic process. Your work will involve a short literature study, hands-on involvement in data collection (EMA via a smartphone app and iTBS sessions in the lab), and initial support of the data analysis. Over time, you'll help document the workflows that link daily-life symptom dynamics to short-term response to stimulation.
 You'll mainly focus on the data-collection (recruitment, running TMS sessions, monitoring EMA compliance) and later on explore preliminary analyses (processing intensive longitudinal data).
 You'll be actively involved in:
 Recruiting and scheduling participants and running EMA and iTBS sessions
 Following predefined TMS procedures (resting motor threshold, Beam F3 localization, delivering the iTBS protocol) under supervision
 Monitoring and managing the EMA data collection and participant compliance
 Contributing to the processing and analysis of intensive longitudinal (EMA) and stimulation data
 Summarizing results and documenting workflows, and collaborating with the research team on interim findings and next steps
 This way, you'll have an influence on the direction of the project and the opportunity to apply and further refine valuable skills at the intersection of neuromodulation, data science, and clinical research.
 What your typical week might look like: 
You'll split your time between the lab and independent work, i.e. running participant sessions (TMS and EMA onboarding), meeting with supervisors to discuss progress and troubleshoot technical or practical challenges, and documenting your workflow and results. Some weeks may be focused on data collection and participant contact, others on managing and interpreting the EMA and stimulation data, or preparing summary reports.

REQUIREMENTS:
Your profile 
You are a motivated recent graduate, with a strong analytical mindset and an interest in neuromodulation, symptom dynamics, and technological innovation in clinical care.
 We are looking for someone who meets the following criteria:
 You recently completed a bachelor’s or master's degree in (neuro-)psychology, social or biomedical sciences, (bio-)engineering, or a related field.
 You have demonstrable affinity with neuroscience and/or human research (e.g. through coursework, your thesis, internship, or previous research projects).
 You are comfortable working with statistical data analysis software or very motivated to learn new tools (e.g. R, STATA, or alternative coding).
 Scientific and/or practical experience with neuroscientific methods such as neuromodulation (TMS) and/or intensive longitudinal/EMA data is not required but is an asset.
 You are eager to take initiative, enjoy solving methodological and practical challenges.
 You collaborate well but can also work independently when running sessions or exploring analyses.
 You are reliable and comfortable in participant-facing tasks, and you handle sensitive data with care.
 You have sufficient proficiency in English to read scientific literature, communicate in a research context, and document your work clearly; proficiency in Dutch is an asset for participant contact.
 Competencies:
 Organizing ability: you can coordinate and keep track of a multimodal data collection (participant scheduling, TMS sessions, and continuous EMA sampling running in parallel), managing the practical logistics.
 Initiative: you take ownership of tasks, identify opportunities for improvement, and follow through independently.
 Accuracy: you pay attention to detail and ensure the quality and traceability of your work.
 Collaboration: you can communicate effectively within a research team and contribute constructively to shared goals.

Are you a systems thinker passionate about bending the curve of biodiversity loss in agricultural landscapes? Are you looking for a meaningful research path with impact on the ground? Are you eager to join a stimulating environment, collaborate across academic fields, and engage with private and public actors? Are you enthusiastic to dive into effective planning and governance arrangements for biodiversity recovery in agricultural landscapes? Do you speak English and Dutch? Then, this PhD position might be the perfect fit for you. 
Biodiversity recovery is essential to sustain resilient food systems, robust businesses, and healthy societies. A transition to a nature-inclusive dairy sector in the Netherlands is pivotal to biodiversity recovery, because of its influence in shaping landscapes through land use and management, and because of its socio-economic relevance. DECISION is a transdisciplinary project involving farmers, dairy companies, financial and service sectors, and local communities, to co-create and accelerate the transition to a resilient and nature-inclusive future. DECISION will count on a broad group of experts, four fully funded PhDs candidates and one postdoc.
For this position, we are looking for a PhD candidate eager to deal with the complexity of public and private governance efforts coming together in landscapes and at farm level, and the need to design coordinated action. In that role, you will build on and integrate the work of your fellow PhD candidates, co-develop a theory of change integrating coordinated public and private action and monitoring, explore synergies and tensions in multi-actor governance and planning, and help bridge research and education.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Develop a Research Proposal and a Training and Supervision Plan, to structure the 5-year project with a 0.8fte PhD trajectory
 Advancing conceptual thinking by linking and comparing business-to-business approaches with collective action and landscape governance
 Conducting and analyzing semi-structured interviews and workshops with stakeholders
 Implement a Theory of Change approach and other approaches for knowledge co-production with stakeholders
 Disseminate results by publishing papers in scientific journals, presenting in international conferences, and creating content items dedicated to stakeholders and students
 Work as a team player, contributing to the activities and wider aims of DECISION project.
 You will work here 
This PhD position will be situated between the Land Use Planning Group of Wageningen University & Research and the Animal Production Systems (APS) group . The LUP group aims to improve our understanding of landscapes as social-ecological systems and focuses on interventions that relieve the pressure on scarce space, improving the overall landscape quality. APS focuses on unravelling the complexity of livestock systems and exploring trade-offs and synergies of innovations regarding environmental impact, animal welfare, and economic viability to design a more sustainable future.
You will be supervised by Dr Judith Westerink (LUP) and Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch (APS). The work of Dr Judith Westerink focuses on transformative landscape governance, in particular related to biodiversity and dairy farming systems. The work of Dr Raimon Ripoll-Bosch focuses on understanding the complex interactions between livestock, nature (biodiversity and ecosystem services) and economy, to design enabling environments for the transitions to nature-inclusive agroecosystems.

REQUIREMENTS:
You have strong analytical skills, capable of disentangling complex problems and understanding diverse perspectives on the matter. You are a responsible and independent researcher, but also a team player that thrives being part of a larger, collaborative and multi-disciplinary team. You are creative, constructive and open to learn from other disciplines.
 You also have: 
 A successfully completed MSc degree in a relevant social science, such as Spatial Planning, Public Administration and Governance, Institutional Economics, Political Science or (Rural) Sociology
 Demonstrated affinity with biodiversity or other environmental topics
 Acquaintance with mixed-method research, experience with conducting and analyzing interviews, surveys and synthesizing documents
 Affinity with inter- and transdisciplinary approaches, and designing interactive sessions with stakeholders
 Excellent writing and presenting skills in English as well as Dutch, for both academic and non-academic audiences
For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

Are you interested in the spatial and socio-cultural interactions between the rural and the urban, how these relate to representations and senses of rural and urban places, and how life course and generational differences may influence this? And would you like to conduct research in an interdisciplinary consortium of Dutch universities, universities of applied sciences and societal partners? Then this postdoc position is perfect for you.
 What are you going to do? 
 The Faculty of Spatial Sciences of the University of Groningen is looking to appoint a postdoctoral researcher “ Socio-Cultural Aspects of Rural-Urban Interactions” . The position is embedded in the NWO KIC research project Fertile Soils for future generations: integrated spatial strategies and effective governance for coherent rural-urban regions. Fertile soils addresses different aspects of rural-urban relations, related to the landscape services they provide. Landscape services are ecosystem services that are offered and consumed within one landscape, such as food production, recreation, biodiversity, flood protection, water retention, space for living, space for economic activities, social cohesion and regional identity. The project consists of 7 work packages. The postdoc Socio-Cultural Aspects of Rural-Urban Interactions is embedded in WP4. WP4 aims to investigate how interactions between rural and urban are experienced in people's daily lives, how they envision these interactions to be in the future, and how this can contribute to a sense of connectedness to the place and/or a regional identity.
 At the Faculty of Spatial Sciences (FSS) the research team includes Tialda Haartsen (professor rural geography, WP4 lead), Charlotte Oosterhuis (PhD, WP4), Jesse Lindenhovius (PhD, WP3), Koen Salemink (supervisor, WP4), Martijn van der Heide and Gunnar Mallon (supervisors, WP3). WP4 also consist of Kristin Zlatanova-Panova (PhD), Jasper de Vries and Marlies Meijer (supervisors) from Wageningen University. FSS is also region-coordinator of the Fertile Soils region Hogeland – city of Groningen. As postdoc, you will perform some of the WP4 research tasks, in close collaboration with the other team members and with the consortium partners in the project.
 These tasks include:
 Investigate rural-urban interactions and socio-cultural meanings of urban and rural areas.
 Explore current and future needs in rural-urban interactions (e.g. regional identity and sense of place) from an intergenerational and life course perspective through representative survey, interviews, and focus group discussions with young societally active groups.
 Relate and integrate the WP4 findings to the other WPs.
 Write academic and popular publications about these research activities.
 PhD supervision.
 Be the contact person for the region Hogeland-Groningen.
 Perform some occasional teaching duties in one of the participating faculties.

REQUIREMENTS:
Our ideal candidate has:
 A PhD degree in a field of study relevant to the topic of the project (e.g. human geography, rural studies or sociology). Completed or to be completed in the near future.
 Strong conceptual thinking skills and a proactive and a proactive and independent work attitude.
 Experience with quantitative and qualitative research methods.
 Publications in international peer-reviewed academic journals that testify of your interest in aspects of rural-urban relations.
 The skills to present academic analyses to varied audiences including scientific professionals and policy makers. Also, you are comfortable building and maintaining a professional network to regional and national policy makers that are affiliated or relevant to the research that you are performing.
  A fluency in English (reading, writing, speaking).
 A fluency in Dutch, as some of the data gathering will take place in this language.

CONTRACT: A temporary appointment of 0.7 FTE for 35 months or 0.8 FTE for 31 months. 
Intended starting date: as soon as possible, but no later than 1 January 2027.

Shape the future of cancer therapy through nanomedicine process engineering. 
 Join as a PhD candidate to design lipid nanoparticles using computational modeling with real-world validation. 
 Job description 
SPARC (Scalable Personalized Nanotherapeutics for Cancer Treatment) is an ambitious research program dedicated to making advanced cancer therapies more effective and accessible, particularly for patients with hard-to-treat “cold tumors.” By developing personalized nanomedicines, SPARC aims to improve patient survival through innovations such as tumor-on-a-chip platforms that reduce reliance on animal testing, and novel manufacturing technologies that enhance therapeutic efficacy and product stability.
As part of this program, we are seeking a highly motivated Ph.D. student with an interest in cross-disciplinary research to join a shared position between the Precision Therapeutics group (Dr. Alina Rwei) in the Chemical Engineering department and the Complex Fluid Processing group (Prof. Johan Padding) in the Process & Energy department of TU Delft. The position will formally be at Precision Therapeutics.
The project is embedded in a strong academic–industrial network and offers close collaboration with leading pharmaceutical partners, including Merck KGaA and Johnson & Johnson.
This project focuses on purification of the output stream of lipid-based drug delivery nanoparticles manufacturing systems. These streams typically contain solvent, lipids and unencapsulated drug components, which need to be removed by dilution and subsequent ultra- or diafiltration. Current purification systems, typically based on (alternating) tangential flow filtration, suffer from loss of expensive lipid nanoparticles and membrane fouling, necessitating expensive regular replacement of the membranes.
Your task will be to engineer innovative purification systems, e.g. by changing membrane materials and designing novel filtration flow geometries, that minimize loss of lipid nanoparticles and maximise throughput. In the design you will explore modularization options for relatively quick and low-cost replacement of filtration system components. The project also involves close interaction with other research teams within the SPARC consortium, e.g., molecular mechanisms for membrane fouling are investigated.
Key Responsibilities
 Computational modelling with CFD simulations: 
 Investigate the flow, diffusion and filtration in tangential flow filtration systems
 Implement correlations to model build-up of fouling and its effects on filtration capacity
 Develop novel flow geometries that balance: 
 Throughput (maximising production rates)
 Mechanical stress on lipid nanoparticles (minimising loss of LNPs)
 Experimental verification
 Experimentally verify the use of alternative membranes for LNP purification.
 Experimentally verify modularisation options for the purification train, including use of quick connectors. 
 Job requirements 
 MSc or equivalent in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Nanotechnology or related field
 Analytical mindset with ability to work across computational and experimental domains
 Have excellent communication skills in English, and want to work in a multidisciplinary team
 Experience in computational fluid dynamics simulations or pharmaceutical downstream processes is a plus

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow.
These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional.
Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

We are looking for a PostDoc who will do research on the intersection of machine learning (ML) and statistics. More specifically, the focus is on the development of algorithmic improvements in causal inference and reinforcement learning through the cross fertilization of machine learning and statistical approaches and applying these innovations in a health setting.
The position is embedded in two projects which act as application domains. First of all, the ten-year gravitation grant Stress in Action, funded through NWO (Dutch National Science Foundation). The goal of the project is to move stress research from the lab into daily life, and hence, the use cases of the methodological innovations will focus on applications to stress-related data, such as wearables, ecological momentary assessments, and other types of questionnaires. Secondly, the ZonMW funded MINMED project which aims to unlock causal effects of interventions in elderly care from observational data.
A variety of academic partners are involved in the two projects, including Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Amsterdam UMC, Erasmus MC, University of Twente, University of Groningen, UMC Groningen, and Utrecht University.
The position is embedded in the Quantitative Data Analytics (QDA) group of the VU in close collaboration with the Amsterdam UMC, Erasmus MC and the University of Groningen. The QDA group focuses on both fundamental and application-driven research in ML.
We are looking for candidates with experience in the area of machine learning or statistics, with a special preference for those with expertise in causal inference and/or reinforcement learning, ideally complemented with a solid background in statistics. We are interested in attracting a PostDoc who is able to perform ground-breaking research on fundamental aspects of machine learning and statistics and wants to apply these innovations in the context of the Stress in Action and MINMED projects.
 Your duties 
The PostDoc position is focused on performing research and contains the following duties:
 performing research in the field of machine learning and publishing in top AI and ML conferences
 participating in the QDA group of VU (lead by Mark Hoogendoorn), the Biostatistics group of Erasmus MC (led by Dimitris Rizopoulos), and Laura Bringmann's intensive longitudinal data lab at the University of Groningen.
 contributing to the Stress in Action and MINMED projects and interacting with the different partners and stakeholders in the project
 contributing to some teaching activities and possibly supervising Bachelor and Master students (20% of the time)

REQUIREMENTS:
We will base our selection on the following components:
 a PhD degree in an area relevant to machine learning and/or statistics
 prior experience in machine learning, ideally also on applications in the health domain, demonstrated by relevant publications
 a strong record of computer programming, with experience in pytorch and/or tensorflow
 demonstrated ability to work both independently and as a team member
As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. We believe that diversity in all its complexity is invaluable for the quality of our teaching, research and service. We are always looking for talent with diverse backgrounds and experiences. This also means that we are committed to creating an inclusive community so that we can use diversity as an asset.
We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. Therefore we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements.

CONTRACT: 18 months

Wil je studenten, promovendi en onderzoekers helpen om wetenschappelijke informatie doelgericht, zorgvuldig en reproduceerbaar te vinden?
Als informatiespecialist educatie bij de Universiteitsbibliotheek Utrecht geef je onderwijs op het gebied van informatievaardigheden en systematisch zoeken. Daarnaast geef je richting aan de manier waarop we omgaan met AI in het zoeken, beoordelen en gebruiken van wetenschappelijke informatie én aan de vertaling daarvan naar ons onderwijs.
 Wat ga je doen? 
Als informatiespecialist adviseer en ondersteun je onderzoekers en studenten binnen Medische Wetenschappen, het UMC Utrecht, Diergeneeskunde en Bètawetenschappen. Met jouw werk draag je direct bij aan de kwaliteit van wetenschappelijk onderzoek en help je studenten om efficiënter en zorgvuldiger met informatie om te gaan. Je doet dit samen met één vaste collega-informatiespecialist: jouw zwaartepunt ligt bij Diergeneeskunde en Bèta, maar het lesgeven, het ontwikkelen van nieuw onderwijs en de intake van aanvragen pakken jullie samen op.
Je verzorgt trainingen in informatievaardigheden voor bachelor- en masterstudenten en trainingen in systematisch zoeken voor promovendi, zowel in groepen als één-op-één. Je ontwikkelt daarvoor nieuw onderwijs en houdt de bestaande leermaterialen actueel, zoals LibGuides, modules en presentaties. Je weet hoe je gericht en systematisch zoekt in de bibliotheekcollectie en in openbare bronnen en bent daarvoor binnen het team het aanspreekpunt. Die kennis breng je op een duidelijke en enthousiasmerende manier over, afgestemd op je publiek: een eerstejaars bachelor vraagt om een ander verhaal dan een promovendus.
Daarnaast begeleid je zoekconsulten en ondersteun je systematic review-projecten: van het scherp krijgen van de vraag tot de zoekstrategie, de documentatie en de peer review van de search. Je legt je werk zo vast dat een ander de zoekactie later kan reproduceren. Ook onderhoud je contact met de facultaire onderwijscoördinatoren, zodat ons aanbod blijft aansluiten op het curriculum, en verbeter je dat aanbod op basis van evaluaties. Het thema AI en systematisch zoeken trek jij. Je test tools zelf uit, vertaalt wat werkt naar onze dienstverlening en draagt bij aan de AI-visie van de afdeling ter ondersteuning van de faculteiten in lijn met onze systematic reviewprojecten.
Je werkt binnen de afdeling Onderwijsondersteuning van de Universiteitsbibliotheek Utrecht. Deze afdeling ontwikkelt en verzorgt onderwijs op het gebied van informatievaardigheden voor alle faculteiten en ondersteunt daarnaast op het gebied van auteursrecht en open leermaterialen. Binnen de afdeling is veel ruimte voor kennisdeling, samenwerking en innovatie. We werken continu aan het verbeteren van ons onderwijsaanbod en spelen in op ontwikkelingen binnen het vakgebied en het onderwijs.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je hebt een academische opleiding.
 Je hebt ruime, aantoonbare ervaring met systematisch zoeken in een academische context: je vertaalt een vage vraag naar concepten, synoniemen en een getoetste zoekstring, en documenteert die zo dat een ander hem een jaar later kan herhalen.
 Je hebt ervaring met het geven van trainingen of andere vormen van het overbrengen van kennis, stemt je verhaal af op het niveau van je publiek en coacht liever dan dat je overneemt: een promovendus vertrekt bij jou met een eigen zoekstrategie.
 Je kunt je goed verplaatsen in het perspectief van de onderzoeker: je hoort ook wat iemand niet zegt en vraagt door totdat de werkelijke informatiebehoefte helder is.
 Je deelt materialen en zoekstrategieën met collega's en maakt je een nieuwe database of tool snel genoeg eigen om die binnen een blok in je onderwijs te gebruiken.
 Je beheerst het Nederlands uitstekend (C1) en het Engels goed (B2).
Verder is het gewenst als je:
 Een achtergrond hebt in de life sciences of ervaring hebt met onderzoek in dat domein;
 Bekend bent met het opzetten en uitvoeren van systematisch reviews en met peer review van zoekstrategieën (bijvoorbeeld PRESS);
 Al met AI-tools voor zoeken hebt gewerkt en daar een onderbouwd oordeel over hebt;
 Ervaring hebt met het ontwikkelen van leermaterialen.

Are you fascinated by the intersection of Physics, Chemistry and materials science? Do you want to contribute to protecting monuments including World Heritage Sites from degradation caused by rising damp?
 The Institute of Physics at the University is seeking an ambitious PhD candidate to investigate the effectiveness of damp-proofing products across multiple length scales.
 Join Us! 
Rising damp from groundwater represents a critical threat to buildings worldwide. Some building-preservation treatments (most of the times polymers) are used to reduce rising damp , that is the moisture uptake from the ground moving upward through porous brick, stone, or mortar by capillary action. These treatments are supposed to create a water-repellent zone in order to interrupt upward moisture transport.
However, the fundamental mechanisms governing the spreading and polycondensation at the microscale, and thus the effectiveness, of such treatments in porous building materials remain largely unexplored. Critical knowledge gaps exist regarding the multiscale behaviour of these treatments, from microscale pore interactions to macroscale building performance.
This project will advance beyond the state of the art by elucidating for the first time the dynamics of spreading and polycondensation of chemical damp proofing products by real-time visualization of these processes at the pore scale. You will use novel experimental methods developed in our laboratory by combining fluorescent viscosity-sensitive probes and confocal/infrared microscopy with mechanical measurements to correlate the microscale of pore interaction to the macroscale behaviour.
Together with a diverse stakeholders group, including chemical product manufacturers, governmental conservation agencies, building asset owners, and contractors, and in collaboration with TU Delft (the Architecture Department) we will establish the knowledge and tools to improve the effectiveness of chemical damp proofing interventions and significantly reduce the estimated €19 million annual costs of chemical treatments in the Netherlands.
Your research will be part of the Soft Matter cluster at the Van der Waals-Zeeman Institute for Experimental Physics (IoP-WZI) at the University of Amsterdam, under the supervision of Prof. Noushine Shahidzadeh (expert on crystallization and sol-gel process in confinement) and Prof. Hannelore Derluyn (expert in micro-CT 3D imaging for porous media).
 This is what you will do 
You will conduct pioneering research combining advanced imaging techniques with experimental characterization to elucidate the effects of different variables on the effectiveness of chemical damp proofing products, with the final goal of increasing the success of such barrier treatments against rising damp in (historic) masonry.
You will Study
 the Rheological changes of the product during polycondensation
 Reaction and aging in quasi-2D micromodels of porous media designed in the lab. Results will bring valuable pore-scale information on gelation and polycondensation, not accessible by other advanced imaging techniques such as NMR and X-ray Computed Tomography (XCT).
 The dynamics of spreading of chemical products at different conditions in different porous materials using fluorescent viscosity-sensitive probes and confocal/infrared microscopy, and also by XCT scans, to get valuable information on the final deposition, following polycondensation at the microscale, and the results on the macroscale behaviour.
 Your core responsibilities include: 
 Conducting independent experimental research at different scales from bulk to confinement under various climatic conditions,
 Performing systematic studies in microfluidic channels and real porous building materials (limestone and sandstone) at the laboratory scale under controlled environmental cycling.
 Using advanced imaging and characterization techniques including optical and electron microscopy, IR and Raman spectroscopy, MRI, and X-ray microtomography to track polycondensation in real time.
 Publishing your findings in peer-reviewed international journals and presenting at international conferences
 Contributing to teaching activities by assisting in undergraduate and master's courses in physics.
 Collaborating with other members of Prof. Shahidzadeh and Prof. Hannelore Derluyn's group and making the link with our collaborator at TUDelft.
 What we ask of you 
 Your experience and profile:

 Strong interest in experimental research combining materials science, sol-gel process, and applications to real-world problems.
 Affinity with experimental techniques including microscopy, spectroscopy, and/or imaging methods.
 Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

How to best incorporate New Genomic Techniques to solve challenging issues in plant breeding? The recent approval by the European Parliament of new legislation to allow application of gene editing approaches in plant breeding, offers new opportunities to address this. One such challenge is to improve complex traits such as crop tolerance to dynamic environmental conditions in the current era of global climate change and how to best incorporate this in plant breeding strategies.
Anticipating the new legislation, the INPROBED project has been granted, which aims to precisely identify and modify cis -regulatory elements and transcription factor genes that control key physiological pathways to specifically adjust targeted gene expression to reshape complex traits.
The project will develop a breakthrough science-enabled technology platform to improve tomato heat, drought and nutrient deficiency tolerance and the nutritional status of tomato fruits for human health. In this project, you will investigate the tomato response to Zn and Fe deficiency and design strategies to improve the Zn/Fe nutritional status of tomatoes for human health.
You will generate dedicated (single-cell) transcriptional data sets feeding into the MNase-defined cistrome occupancy (MOA-seq) analysis of transcription factor binding of tomato promoter elements controlling the Zn and Fe deficiency responsive gene expression. You will design specific constructs to edit transcription factor genes and their target promoters, and analyse the effects of optimized gene expression regulation on plant performance under optimal and field-like conditions at the Netherlands Plant Eco-phenotyping Centre. Your research aims to improve tomato Zn and Fe uptake under regular field conditions and to enhance the Zn and Fe nutritional status of tomato fruits.
INPROBED is part of the prestigious European Innovation Council (EIC) Pathfinder Challenge programme addressing innovative biotechnology for climate resilient crops. It brings together excellent expertise from world-leading European research institutions and companies. You will work closely together with researchers across the consortium to predict and edit targeted gene promoters, to design relevant constructs for gene editing and to evaluate the gene-edited plants to establish this topic firmly into the plant breeding domain.
Within Wageningen University, you will be embedded in the Laboratory of Genetics of the Plant Sciences Group, and collaborate with researchers and thesis students investigating the genetic basis of plant adaptation to the environment, focusing on plant nutrition, metal tolerance and photosynthesis. Your research is expected to deliver fundamental insights into the genetic regulation of tomato gene expression and provide strong experimental validation of the technology platform to improve complex crop traits through gene editing of gene expression regulators.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 To design the experimental setup for gene expression analysis of tomato response to Zn and Fe deficiency, and of Zn and Fe loading into the developing fruit.
 The biological interpretation of MOA-seq analysis with respect to the tomato response to Zn and Fe deficiency.
 The experimental validation of gene-edited tomato plants with respect to plant growth and development and their ionome under optimal, natural and mineral-stress conditions.
 To establish a fruitful collaboration with international partners in the project and to supervise a part-time technician on the project.
 To write manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals reporting on the results of your research.
 Your team 
You will work with international partners in the project and with other members in the Botanical Genetics team of the Laboratory of Genetics of Wageningen University, which is led by Prof. Mark Aarts You will work in close collaboration with a technician to be appointed on the project.
 You will work here 
Wageningen UR has a global reputation for its ground-breaking research and innovative education in the fields of food and health, sustainable agrosystems, the rural environment, and societal development - all of which make an essential contribution to the quality of life, i.e. the supply of safe and healthy food and drink, on the one hand, and the chance to live, work and play in a balanced ecosystem with a large variety of plants and animals on the other. Within Wageningen UR, the Plant Sciences Group brings together science education and scientific, strategic and applied research in the fields of biology, of plants in relation to their environment, of plant-related organisms and of plant production. The Laboratory of Genetics is interested in heredity in general, in particular the origin, architecture and consequences of genetic variation of a wide range of organisms across the biological kingdoms.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are an ambitious, curiosity-driven and collaboration-oriented plant scientist, with:
 a strong academic track record and a PhD in plant biotechnology, plant molecular genetics or a related topic;
 experience with plant mineral homeostasis and/or tomato research;
 demonstrated expertise in the analysis of large data-sets;
 a strong interest in experimental research;
 an excellent oral and written English communication skills.
In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level C1 .

CONTRACT: 30 months
